original_question: Let M_S be the spherical maximal operator on R^d, defined by taking at each x the supremum over r > 0 of the average of |f| on the sphere S^{d-1}(x,r). For dimensions d >= 2, is M_S bounded as an operator from W^{1,p}(R^d) to W^{1,p}(R^d) throughout the full endpoint range 1 < p <= d/(d-1)?
target_in_paper: Section 3.2, Question 5: the open problem on whether the centered spherical maximal operator remains bounded on Sobolev spaces in the unresolved range 1 < p <= d/(d-1).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right object (the centered spherical maximal operator on R^d), the right ambient space (Sobolev spaces W^{1,p}(R^d)), the right dimensional regime (d >= 2), and the right unresolved exponent range (1 < p <= d/(d-1)). It also asks the correct type of question: extension of the known boundedness beyond the Stein-Bourgain range.
missing_details: The paper defines the operator as the centered spherical maximal operator S via normalized surface averages over spheres S^{d-1}(x,r) with respect to the canonical surface measure dσ; that normalization should be stated explicitly.
The centeredness should be made explicit, even though it is implicit in your notation.
The quantifiers should be stated explicitly: for every dimension d >= 2 and every exponent 1 < p <= d/(d-1).
'Bounded' should be spelled out as the existence of a constant C = C(d,p) such that ||Sf||_{W^{1,p}(R^d)} <= C ||f||_{W^{1,p}(R^d)} for all f in W^{1,p}(R^d).
The question is the global Euclidean one on R^d, not the local-domain variant S_Ω discussed elsewhere in the literature.
The paper immediately notes that p = 1 is excluded: S is not bounded from W^{1,1}(R^d) to L^1(R^d), so that endpoint is not part of the problem.
To be fully paper-faithful, it helps to indicate that boundedness is already known for p > d/(d-1), and the question asks whether that known result extends to the remaining range 1 < p <= d/(d-1).
refined_question: For each dimension d >= 2, let S be the centered spherical maximal operator on R^d defined by S f(x) = sup_{r>0} (1/σ(S^{d-1}(x,r))) ∫_{S^{d-1}(x,r)} |f(y)| dσ(y), where dσ is the canonical surface measure on the sphere S^{d-1}(x,r). Is it true that for every 1 < p <= d/(d-1) there exists a constant C = C(d,p) such that ||S f||_{W^{1,p}(R^d)} <= C ||f||_{W^{1,p}(R^d)} for all f in W^{1,p}(R^d)?
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in arXiv:1912.04625. Section 2 defines the spherical maximal operator and recalls that, by Stein-Bourgain L^p boundedness together with the Sobolev result for translation-commuting sublinear operators, S is already bounded on W^{1,p}(R^d) when p > d/(d-1). Section 3.2 then isolates the remaining open case as Question 5, attributed to Hajłasz and Onninen. The sentence immediately after Question 5 explicitly excludes p = 1 by noting a counterexample to boundedness from W^{1,1} to L^1. So your draft is very close, but to be fully stand-alone and paper-faithful it should specify the normalized spherical-average definition, the universal quantifiers in d and p, the exact norm inequality meant by boundedness, and the explicit exclusion of p = 1.
